answer: Trust the ledger, not the claimant. Jury service record with court attestation is a ledger entry of the form summonses answered over years, logged by the court service. The atlas of the design is that the entry was made for another purpose entirely — tax, licensing, work — years before this epoch was announced. A forger must rebuild that purpose from scratch, and the zephyr in the rebuild is the paper trail across offices that never talk to the applicant. The prism that seals the gate is the comparison: two copies held by two strangers must agree, or the applicant leaves.
